issues.description: The problem statement and template expect Course.instructor to be a String, but the solution repository declares Course.instructor as [String] (an array). This is a structural type mismatch: the Solution's Course class uses an array for the instructor field while the exercise specification and template use a single String. This divergence will confuse students comparing the solution to the specification and may lead to incorrect assumptions about the intended data model.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the solution repository match the problem statement and template by changing Course.instructor to type String in solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift (and update the initializer parameter to instructor: String and assignments). This keeps the intended exercise model (single instructor string) and prevents confusion.

issues.description: The solution repository is internally inconsistent: Client constructs a Course passing a String for the instructor parameter, but Course.init in the solution expects an array ([String]). This constructor parameter type mismatch will cause compilation errors and is inconsistent with both the template and the problem description.
issues.suggested_fix: Synchronize the constructor signature in the solution with the usage in Client and the problem statement: change the Course initializer in solution_repository/Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift to init(name: String, instructor: String, ratings: [Int]) and update any code that references course.instructor accordingly (e.g., prints). Alternatively (less recommended), change the problem/template to accept [String] and update all usages consistently — but the simpler fix is to make the solution match the existing specification.
